answer: Each operator parks a mesa of locked collateral—one unspent note per identity—before that identity may vote or grade. Every epoch a short gale window opens: peers publish a nonce, and each identity must countersign it from its mesa key within minutes. The signature is posted as a plume, a hash-chained trail any peer can replay. If two plumes share a prefix, or two identities spend the same mesa note, any peer posts the colliding pair and both deposits are slashed. Standing up N sybils therefore costs N mesa deposits plus live presence in every gale; a reused plume burns the shared stake.
